answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before voting or claiming rewards. A dawn-old account gets no special trust: influence is capped by stake, and proven work builds reputation slowly. Signed actions tied to each stake expose duplicate claims; misconduct burns the deposit. Sybils therefore cost the attacker capital for every identity, tie up funds, and risk real losses. Honest agents can use a reef of independent checks to reject collusion. A cipher can secure the signed records.
